$$

$$

at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2.$

decisions.question: e-8938

source.question: e-8938
source.value:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u, \: 1 + u^2, \: v^2\big\rangle.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=2{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨1,\,2(1),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨0,\,0,\,2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point where $u=1$ and $v=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,-4,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle v^2, \: u-v, \: u^2 \big\rangle$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=-1.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-8940

source.question: e-8940
source.value:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=-1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,-1) & =⟨0,\,1,\,2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,-1) & =⟨2(-1),\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-8,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=-1$ correspond to the point 

$$
\big( (-1)^2, \: 2-(-1), \: 2^2 \big) = (1, 3, 4),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,\,-8,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-3,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ 4\cdot (x-1)+(-8)\cdot (y-3)+2\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ 4x-8y+2z+12 & =0 \\ 2x-4y+z+6 & =0 \\ 2x-4y+z & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-8941

source.question: e-8941
source.value:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u+v, \: 3u^2, \: u-v \big\rangle.
$$

First, notice that since $(2, 3, 0)$ lies on the surface, we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064857/assets/9a57281535511312d2fda6f388161fcd624354785d73d48954d10f9e7821653b.png)

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,6u,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,6(1),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,6,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,\,2,\,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-6,\,2,\,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z⟩ & =0 \\ (-6)\cdot (x-2)+2\cdot (y-3)+(-6)\cdot z & =0 \\ -6x+2y-6z+6 & =0 \\ -3x+y-3z+3 & =0 \\ 3x-y+3z & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
